checks.title: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology — Thermal Control
locators: §7.1 Introduction, equation (1) and bullets for environmental input, internally generated, radiated and stored heat
checks.notes: The source supports separate absorbed, generated, radiated and stored terms. The model consistently uses whole-boundary watts and sets stored heat to zero; its temperature is a steady-state estimate, not survival evidence. The source figure caption mixes heat/flux terminology; the atlas does not import that caption as a unit convention.
checks.statement: Spacecraft heat balance separates environmental absorption, internal heat, radiation and stored thermal energy.
checks.exclusions: The explorer sets stored thermal energy to zero; equilibrium is not a transient temperature or evidence of cold survival.

checks.title: NASA Delay/Disruption Tolerant Networking Overview
locators: What is DTN? store-and-forward definition; How Does DTN Work?, first paragraph; CFDP distinction
checks.notes: The primary description supports retaining data when onward forwarding is unavailable. The atlas only borrows buffering across interrupted contacts; it does not implement the bundle protocol, CFDP or an RF link budget.
checks.statement: retain data for later transfer across contact interruptions.
checks.exclusions: The one-hop reliable acknowledgement abstraction is not DTN/CFDP or proof of an RF or optical link.

checks.title: NASA NEPP Single Event Effect Criticality Analysis
locators: §4.3 SEE Rate Calculations, printed pp.28–30; particle distribution, chord-length geometry, cross-section and device-versus-bit rate conventions
checks.notes: The source combines device response, particle distribution and sensitive geometry. It warns about assumptions and uncertainty. Effective angle-integrated reset flux is an authored reduction; no per-steradian flux is silently substituted.
checks.statement: Single-event rate estimation depends on environment, device response and geometry.
checks.exclusions: The effective angle-integrated flux × reset cross-section × device count is synthetic; it is not an environment, shielding or mission-survival calculation.

checks.title: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook — Poisson Distribution
checks.notes: Setting the event count to zero gives exp(-mu). Here mu=rate×duration under an explicit independent constant-rate assumption. The probability does not drive scripted faults or multiply retained work.
checks.statement: Poisson zero-event probability exp(−λT) for the assumed constant independent rate.
checks.exclusions: The probability is context only; scripted resets drive the trace. It must not multiply retained products and double-count losses.
